title: Lean a ladder at a safe angle
instruction: Lean the ladder against the wall at a safe angle for climbing.
context: OSHA's construction rule for portable ladders, 29 CFR 1926.1053(b)(5)(i), requires a ladder that is not self-supporting to be set so the horizontal distance from its top support to its foot is approximately one quarter of its working length, the length along the ladder from the foot to the top support. That is about 75.5 degrees from the floor. Steeper, a ladder can tip over backward; shallower, its foot can slide out. The instruction says only "a safe angle". Done by: construction laborers, roofers and painters.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. In front of the right arm, 10.5 cm in from its base toward the midline, a fixed grey wooden wall (30 mm deep, 160 mm wide, 120 mm tall) stands across the arms' reach, its face 30 cm out from the bases. A yellow pine ladder, a bar 160 x 40 x 15 mm and 60 g, stands upright on its end on the table, 1 mm off the wall's face, its 40 mm side along the wall, its top about 40 mm above the wall.
scoring: The ladder leans when its foot's lowest corner is within 2 mm of the table, the nearest point of its face toward the wall is within 3 mm of the wall's top edge, it faces the wall (its 40 mm side level and along the wall, each within 10 degrees), and its centre is within the wall's 160 mm width. 1.0 when it leans at 72.5 to 78.5 degrees from the table (cos 0.20 to 0.30: the foot out a quarter of the length, give or take 5 percentage points) and is still for 1 s, which ends the trial. 0.5 when it leans at 69.5 to 72.5 or 78.5 to 81.4 degrees (cos 0.15 to 0.20 or 0.30 to 0.35). 0 otherwise: upright, lying flat, beside the wall, or leaning outside those angles.
reset_notes: Stand the ladder back upright on its end against the wall's face.
fidelity: The ladder is a plain bar at about 1/25 scale, with no rungs or feet. The 4 to 1 rule fixes an angle, so it holds at any scale. The top rests on the wall's top edge, as on a roof edge, not against a face. The ladder and wall have rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) and the table the simulator's default (0.5), so a ladder that would slide out in reality may hold in the sim. The scorer checks the angle, not whether it slides.
